title: Slice 2: glyph impact, a transitive blast radius with --ref
description: DEC-216 (opum-doc, 2026-10-20), Q2 and Q4, to the six acceptance criteria in the 2026-10-20 design-readiness review's section 3 (opum-doc docs/research/market/evidence/2026-10-20-glyph-cli/design-readiness.md). Adds glyph impact <symbol> [--depth N] [--all] [--ref <ref>] [--json] over the existing symbol and call graph: a transitive reverse closure with a deterministic shortest path, bounded depth, honest truncation and unresolved sites, and a ref-pinned index. Builds on slice 1's command contract. Requested by opum-agent for ODOC-487.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `glyph impact <symbol>` returns every transitive caller within the default depth of 5, each caller once, with its depth, one shortest path to the target and the call sites on that path; direct callers are depth 1; when several shortest paths exist a total order (path string, then file, line, column) picks one, so the answer is deterministic.

`--depth <n>` bounds the traversal and `--all` runs the full closure; a truncated answer reports `truncated: true` with the number of callers left unexplored; a cycle terminates and is marked `cycle: true`.
`--ref <ref>` indexes that commit's tree without a checkout; a dirty working tree never changes a `--ref` answer, and the working-tree mode remains the default for interactive use.

`--json` emits one envelope of kind `impact.result` carrying the selected symbol, callers by depth, `resolvedSites`, `unresolvedSites`, `truncated` and cache status; the same repository state and ref yield byte-identical JSON apart from the `cache` field; an ambiguous name exits 2 with its candidates and an unknown symbol exits 3.

Tests cover a fixture chain a -> b -> c -> d (d's impact includes c at 1, b at 2, a at 3), an unrelated symbol (empty, not an error), a cycle, an ambiguous name, a not-found symbol, and a dirty tree with and without `--ref`.
`glyph callers` and `glyph diff` do not change their answers; `bun run check` passes; README and an ADR or decision record name the semantics, the depth default and the precision caveat.

plan: Record the plan on GCLI-10 in a tracker-only PR off dev; do not claim the task and do not create a code branch until the operator approves the item on the next daily plan and the orchestrator relays it.
Design basis: ADR 0003 names DEC-216 Q2/Q4 and DEC-216 (a1) for module-scope call sites; README states the semantics, the depth default of 5 and the precision caveat.

Traversal (new src/impact.ts): reverse BFS over index.sites, each symbol once at its shortest depth; one shortest path per caller chosen by the total order (path string, then file, line, column); callers sorted by (depth, path string, file, line, column).

Honest bounds: traverse the full closure even when --depth N is given; emit depth <= N, set truncated when any depth exceeds N, and report unexplored as the exact count of those; --all is unbounded; each symbol is discovered once so cycles terminate, and SCCs mark a caller cycle:true with envelope-level cycle when any exists.
Module scope per DEC-216 (a1): each module-scope call site is a terminal depth-1 caller with symbol null and a one-site path, never expanded, so impact's depth-1 set is a superset of callers.

Ref-pinned index (new src/snapshot.ts): --ref resolves to a commit (not_found/3 when unresolvable), lists regular blobs with git ls-tree -r -z, reads them with one git cat-file --batch, and builds the program on an in-memory compiler host that serves paths under the repo root only from the ref map (tsconfig and extends included) and falls back to ts.sys only outside it; cache key is index format plus ref sha plus file list; the working tree stays the default; Q4's diff-requires---ref is deferred to the code-map slice in ADR 0003.

Surface: glyph impact <symbol> [--depth N] [--all] [--ref <ref>] [--json], kind impact.result, exit codes 0/1/2/3/7 in the COMMANDS registry; ambiguous name = usage/2 with candidates, unknown symbol = not_found/3, unknown ref = not_found/3, bad depth or --depth with --all = usage/2, Git refusal = indeterminate/7; callers and diff answers unchanged.

Envelope: {symbol, ref or null, callers, cycle, truncated, unexplored, resolvedSites, unresolvedSites, totals, index}; resolvedSites = index.sites.length and unresolvedSites = index.unresolvedSites (index-wide, because the index retains no unresolved callee identities); repeated runs are byte-identical apart from index.cache.

Tests: test/impact.test.ts (chain a->b->c->d with depths 1/2/3, unrelated symbol empty, equal-length path tie-break, cycle, exact unexplored count, module-scope entry), ref-tree tests (dirty tree, file deleted in the checkout, tsconfig at the ref), cli e2e (text and JSON, --depth, --all, ambiguous, unknown symbol, unknown ref, bad depth, repeat-run identity, cache hit), contract goldens and the program walk, each with a positive control.

Docs and delivery: ADR 0003 and README through pinned lore 0.13.0 with lore check exit 0; bun run check; PR to dev with Docs, Tracker integrity and Check green on the exact head; report the head and a review worktree; land only on the orchestrator's word.

Scope read: full PR diff, src/impact.ts, src/snapshot.ts, src/program.ts, src/git.ts, src/discover.ts, src/cache.ts, src/indexer.ts, src/contract.ts, src/types.ts, src/queries.ts, src/errors.ts, test/impact.test.ts, test/cli.test.ts, test/contract.test.ts, ADR 0002/0003, README, CLAUDE.md, docs/log.md; plus node_modules/typescript@5.9.3 createCompilerHostWorker.

Nothing I found is a traversal or envelope correctness bug: AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5 and AC6 are met with tests that would go red, and AC3 is met for every tracked source. The blocker for me is that AC3's absolute claim is knowingly false in one place and the ADR settles it locally rather than routing it.

FINDINGS

1. MAJOR — `--ref` reads in-repo `node_modules` from disk, beyond both the ruling and the approved plan. src/snapshot.ts:97,103,113,117,137. Any path containing a `node_modules` segment that the commit's tree does not contain falls back to `ts.sys`, i.e. to the checkout. That makes AC3's "a dirty working tree never changes a `--ref` answer" literally false, and it contradicts the plan opum-doc accepted verbatim on GCLI-10 ("serves paths under the repo root only from the ref map (tsconfig and extends included) and falls back to ts.sys only outside it"). The consequence is real, not theoretical: node_modules content changes module resolution, so it can move `unresolvedSites` and, where a library type is what lets a call resolve to an in-repo declaration, the caller set itself. Two machines with different installed dependencies can answer the same `--ref` differently. README:205-209 and ADR 0003:85-88 disclose it honestly, but the ADR is the writer's own record — this is a design deviation that needs opum-doc's ruling (restrict the fallback to the TypeScript stdlib path, which is already served by the outside-root branch, or bless the exception explicitly). Note also that the writer's claim to you ("node_modules is the only disk fallback") is imprecise: paths outside the repo root also go to disk (snapshot.ts:94,101,107), so a parent-directory tsconfig via `extends`, a hoisted `node_modules`, or an `import "../shared/x"` out of the repo is read from the filesystem too — see finding 9. I verified the host otherwise cannot read the checkout: TS 5.9.3's createCompilerHostWorker has no `getSourceFileByPath`, so the overridden `getSourceFile`/`readFile`/`fileExists`/`directoryExists`/`getDirectories`/`readDirectory`/`realpath`/`getCurrentDirectory` are the ones createProgram uses (typescript.js:126251-126293), and every in-repo non-node_modules path is served from `docs` or not at all.

2. MINOR — module-scope callers are reported deeper than the approved plan says. src/impact.ts:201-206, test/impact.test.ts:145-165. The plan (and (a1)'s wording) says "each module-scope call site is a terminal depth-1 caller with symbol null and a one-site path"; the code reports a module site that calls an intermediate at its true depth with a multi-site path (test asserts depth 2, path length 2). I think the code is the better answer — it is terminal, it does not hide anything, and depth-1 remains a superset of `callers` — but ADR 0003:73-77 ("its own depth") records the extension in the writer's own record, so it should be confirmed with opum-doc rather than settled here. Flagged for the same routing as finding 1.

3. MINOR — an ambiguous name tells the user to use a flag `impact` does not have. src/program.ts:304 passes `undefined` as the file pattern into resolveSymbol, whose error at src/queries.ts:40 says "narrow with --file". `impact` declares only --depth/--all/--ref (program.ts:295-299, contract.ts:85-100), so a duplicated name has no disambiguation path at all and the advice is dead. AC4 is met (exit 2 with candidates, test/cli.test.ts:265-276) but the message is wrong. Either add `--file` to `impact` or give resolveSymbol a caller-supplied remedy line.

4. MINOR — the human cycle line is wrong in two cases. src/program.ts:337 prints "cycle: at least one caller can reach itself through this symbol". (i) A self-recursive target prints no callers ("(none)") and then that line, contradicting itself, even though ADR 0003:70-72 explicitly describes the recursive-target case. (ii) `cyclicSymbols` is an SCC over the whole discovered subgraph (impact.ts:233-239), so a caller-only cycle (a↔b, b→target) marks a and b, neither of which reaches itself "through this symbol". ADR:69 states the same over-claim. The JSON `cycle` flags are consistent and harmless; the sentence is not. No CLI test covers a cycle's text output.

5. MINOR — ADR 0003:118-120 says a dependency version change "can therefore change a `--ref` answer". It cannot while the entry is cached: computeRefKey (src/cache.ts:67-73) hashes format+sha+file list and nothing from node_modules, and loadIndex (program.ts:105) returns the cached index without rebuilding. Either the key is wrong for the documented exception or the consequence sentence is. Cheapest honest fix is the sentence; the pre-existing working-tree key has the same property, so I would not call it a new bug.

6. MINOR — `--all` and the default depth of 5 are not exercised by data that needs them. Every impact fixture (the CLI IMPACT_FILES and the CHAIN) is 3 hops deep, i.e. shallower than the default, so `--all` answers identically to no flag (test/cli.test.ts:233-238 asserts only `depth: {bound: null}` and `test/impact.test.ts:57-75` likewise). A regression that made `--all` set bound=5, or that made the default 3, would pass everything except the literal `{bound: 5}` expectation at cli.test.ts:188. One 7-hop chain asserting default → truncated:true/unexplored:2 and `--all` → all 6 would close AC1's "within the default depth of 5" and AC2's "--all runs the full closure" properly.

7. MINOR — the tie-break replacement branch is never executed by the tests. src/impact.ts:221-224 is reachable only when a later-expanded depth-(k-1) parent of the same caller has a lexicographically smaller path string than the first (site position order and symbol-id order differ, so it is reachable), and it is the branch that actually implements AC1's total order. The tie-break test (test/impact.test.ts:86-104) has the first-discovered candidate already win, so deletion of the branch would not fail it. Related: the determinism test compares two runs and two cache states but never permutes `index.sites`/`index.symbols`, so an implementation that leaked index insertion order would still be byte-identical. Cloning the index with reversed arrays and asserting equality would prove what the AC actually claims.

8. NIT — `resolvedSites`/`unresolvedSites` are never asserted by value (test/cli.test.ts:197-198: `>0` and `typeof "number"`). The stated interpretation (resolved = index.sites.length, unresolved = index.unresolvedSites) is exactly the kind of thing an off-by-one would slip through. AC4 only says "carrying", so this is a test-strength note, not a failure.

9. NIT — README:203-209 says "Paths the tree does not contain are invisible to that program ... The one exception is `node_modules`". In-repo non-node_modules paths are indeed invisible, but paths outside the repo root are read from disk (snapshot.ts:94,101,107), and that is where a parent `tsconfig.json` reached by `extends`, a hoisted dependency tree, or a `../` import lives. Worth one clause so the "one exception" is accurate.

10. NIT — determinism rests on `localeCompare` with no locale argument (src/impact.ts:73,83; same pattern pre-exists in src/queries.ts:17). On one machine it is stable; across machines with different ICU default locales the ordering — and therefore the byte-identical claim at AC4 — is not guaranteed. A plain codepoint comparison, or a pinned locale, would make the guarantee unconditional.

11. NIT — a `--ref` cache hit still reads the whole tree first. loadIndex calls snapshotAtRef (program.ts:100) before consulting the cache, so ls-tree plus cat-file of every source and every `.json` blob (snapshot.ts:29-31 includes .json, so a package-lock.json of tens of MB) runs even on a hit. The hit saves only the TS program. Since the sha already determines the tree, and the file list is redundant for keying by the function's own comment (cache.ts:64-66), the key could be computed without the read.

12. NIT — the root command description still says "what calls this symbol, and which symbols a diff touches" (src/program.ts:238), omitting impact. README and HELP_EPILOGUE include it.

Answers to your specific questions

(b) The total order is total. compareCallers (impact.ts:81-89) keys on depth, then the path string, then the first edge's position; path strings are unique per discovery (nodes[0] is a symbol id, unique in the index, or a `module:file:line:column` key, unique per site), so no tie can fall through to insertion order. The first-edge position clause is only reachable for two sites of the same caller-and-callee, where it correctly picks the earlier site. BFS layer order guarantees every equal-depth candidate arrives before the symbol is popped, so a replacement is never followed by a stale expansion — the claim in the file's header comment holds. Byte identity: the envelope carries no timestamp or path-dependent field beyond `ref` as written, `byDepth` is depth-sorted, and the cold-vs-warm-cache comparison at cli.test.ts:208-212 is a real two-build comparison. Only the locale caveat (finding 10) and the untested order-independence (finding 7) qualify it.

(c) Truncation is exact: the whole closure is traversed unconditionally and `unexplored` counts entries in `all` beyond the bound (impact.ts:243-254), so `truncated === (unexplored > 0)` by construction, no frontier estimate. Cycles terminate because a symbol is enqueued only on first discovery (impact.ts:217-220); SCC marking via iterative Kosaraju (impact.ts:96-163) is correct, including self-loops and the target; module-scope entries are correctly never in a cycle.

(d) Beyond finding 1, I could not find an in-repo working-tree read on the `--ref` path. rootNames come only from the tree's blob list, the tsconfig is looked for at the repository root in the snapshot only (discover.ts:162-170), `extends` resolves through the snapshot host, and node_modules is the sole in-repo fallback. The leak that remains is real though: the working-tree `node_modules` can change `unresolvedSites` and potentially resolution, and there is no test that puts a `node_modules` in a fixture to demonstrate either that independence or its absence.

(e) The index-wide interpretation is internally consistent and matches Q2's "unresolvedSites is always reported": both fields are present on every envelope including an empty or truncated answer, and ADR:96-99 plus README:82-85 state index-wide explicitly. The one place the honesty is thin is the human line at src/program.ts:339, "unresolved: N of M call site(s) did not resolve", printed directly beneath a caller list without "in this index"; a reader can take it as scoped to the closure. The JSON is unambiguous; the text could say "index-wide".

(f) The CLAUDE.md change is purely descriptive: it extends the "What other repositories read from here" file list with src/impact.ts and src/snapshot.ts (CLAUDE.md:86-90) and touches no CI, dependency, lockfile, hook, release, pin or settings path, and nothing inside a managed block. It does not tighten anything. One unrelated staleness in the same list caught my eye but is not this PR's: CLAUDE.md:96 still says "exit 0/1/2/3" although the family has carried 7 since slice 1.

NEW FINDINGS

1. MINOR — readBlobs fails open on a missing object. src/git.ts:139-145: a header of `<oid> missing` / `<oid> ambiguous` hits `continue`, and src/snapshot.ts:115-116 then drops any entry whose text is undefined. The comment at git.ts:142-144 states the intended behaviour ("an indeterminate repository, not a miss") but the code treats it as a miss. Consequence: in a corrupt object store, or a partial (`--filter=blob:none`) clone whose promisor remote is unreachable, a blob the tree lists is silently omitted from the --ref index, `unresolvedSites` is not incremented (the file is never walked), and the command exits 0 with a short answer — in exactly the mode whose promise is that an empty answer is not read as "no impact". It is also persistent: program.ts:102-106 keys the cache from the listing alone, so the incomplete index is written and served under the full-tree key. Fix: throw indeterminateError from readBlobs instead of `continue` (or return the missing ids and have snapshotAtRef throw), and add a unit test with a fabricated `missing` header. I rate it MINOR because no healthy repository reaches it and no acceptance criterion is compromised, but it is the one place in the new code where a wrong answer is silent.
2. MINOR — the README's impact transcript is stale. README:68 prints `unresolved: 0 of 3 call site(s) did not resolve; an empty answer is not proof of no impact`, but src/program.ts:343 prints `coverage (index-wide): 3 resolved call site(s); 0 call-shaped site(s) did not resolve; an empty answer is not proof of no impact`, and test/cli.test.ts:222 pins "coverage (index-wide):" in the real output. Fix: replace the line in the transcript with the current one.
3. Fix: both to "terminal at its true depth with its full path", citing (a2). The behaviour is right; only the specs in the code are wrong, and a reader of impact.ts would conclude the file violates its own ruling.
4. MINOR — the "two machines answer identically" claim is absolute, and the cache cannot see outside-root reads. ADR 0003:126-135 and README:206-212 say two machines with different installs answer the same commit identically and that a fully dirty checkout cannot influence a --ref answer; src/cache.ts:61-65 says the SHA and the index format "determine the derived index". But src/snapshot.ts:126/133/139/149/168 delegate every outside-root path to ts.sys — the ADR's own Decision bullet (:95-99) names the hoisted dependency tree and a parent tsconfig reached via `extends` as living there — and computeRefKey (cache.ts:67-73) includes nothing from them.
